stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of Meta-Llama-3-8B on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It is categorized under key AI/ML domains including transformers, llama, and text-generation.
This indicates ongoing community interest and evaluation of Meta's latest open-source model releases.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It points to the use of standard NLP pipelines, specifically 'text-generation'.
The model is categorized under key ML technologies like 'transformers' and 'llama'.

stories.title: Europe’s AI labeling and transparency rules are now in effect
stories.author: Jess Weatherbed
bullet_points: The EU's AI Act mandates new transparency rules regarding AI usage.
Companies must now disclose when users are interacting with AI models like chatbots.
The rules also require labeling of AI-generated content, such as deepfakes, online.

stories.title: China’s Alibaba takes another swipe at America’s AI supremacy
stories.author: Robert Hart
bullet_points: Alibaba has launched Qwen3.8-Max, claiming it is their most capable AI model to date.
The company asserts that Qwen3.8-Max rivals leading US models from Anthropic and OpenAI.
This development signals a significant competitive challenge to US dominance in the frontier AI space.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the DeepSeek-R1 model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized under text-generation and conversational AI pipelines.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors, indicating a focus on practical deployment.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has secured significant funding, raising $88 million.
The funding round includes major investors such as Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama is rapidly growing, currently serving 8.9 million developers in the open models space.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) utilizing MLX.
Speed improvements reach up to 90% faster when running with coding agents, based on the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance boost results in faster response times and reduced memory usage for LLMs.
Model output quality has also seen an improvement following the MLX engine update.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new model architecture.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, offering an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The key feature is its 'local-first' design, allowing AI to run entirely on user hardware.
It integrates native support for Ollama, making local LLM deployment seamless for personal AI.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for optimized performance.
This integration specifically targets Apple Silicon hardware, enhancing local AI capabilities on Macs.
The feature is currently available in a preview build, signaling ongoing optimization and adoption.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed to integrate with messaging applications.
It utilizes local AI coding agents, emphasizing on-device processing for privacy and control.
The tool leverages Ollama, indicating a focus on running open-source models locally.

stories.title: Microsoft is bringing Xbox 360 games to PC
stories.author: Tom Warren
bullet_points: Microsoft is expanding its PC gaming initiative to include Xbox 360 titles.
The plan allows third-party developers to port their Xbox 360 games to PC.
This follows Microsoft's prior announcement regarding the porting of original Xbox games to PC.

stories.title: TokTier: Exact Stateful Tokenization for Agentic LLM Serving
stories.author: Zhichao Cao
bullet_points: TokTier addresses the inefficiency of re-tokenizing full request texts in LLM serving systems, especially for agentic workflows.
The core problem is that appending small tool results to long transcripts often forces re-tokenization due to token boundary shifts.
Empirical data shows that while most calls append significant context (median 1.4K chars), session restarts remain a major bottleneck.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
Integration with llama.cpp expands the range of supported models and hardware capabilities.
The update augments Ollama's MLX engine, particularly benefiting Apple silicon users.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for subagents within Claude Code.
The update also enables web search functionality within the Claude Code environment.
This enhances the capabilities of AI coding assistants by adding complex reasoning and real-time data access.

stories.title: As Reddit stock falls, CEO questions value of Google's AI Overviews
stories.author: Samuel Axon
bullet_points: Reddit is reportedly reconsidering its licensing agreement with Google.
The CEO of Reddit has publicly questioned the value proposition of Google's AI Overviews.
The news links Reddit's stock performance to its strategic relationship with Google's AI initiatives.

stories.title: Defcon's new badge is a security key you can see inside
stories.author: Kim Zetter, wired.com
bullet_points: Defcon's new badge incorporates a removable chip for enhanced security.
The chip design allows hackers to inspect the badge's contents.
The badge retains functionality even after the Defcon event, posing a potential risk.

stories.title: ExtractBench: A Benchmark for Schema-Guided Enterprise Document Extraction
stories.author: Simon Suo
bullet_points: Introduces ExtractBench, a new benchmark specifically designed for schema-guided enterprise document extraction.
This benchmark uniquely evaluates multiple critical metrics simultaneously: value accuracy, record completeness, grounding, and operational cost.
It addresses the growing industry need for AI agents to reliably extract structured data from complex enterprise documents according to predefined schemas.

stories.title: AgentHPOBench: A Benchmark For Evaluating LLM Agents as Sequential Hyperparameter Optimizers
stories.author: Xuanjing Huang
bullet_points: Introduces AgentHPOBench, a new benchmark designed to evaluate LLM agents' capability as sequential hyperparameter optimizers.
Addresses a gap in current LLM evaluation by focusing on an agent's ability to interpret experimental evidence and guide subsequent decisions, rather than just static output.
Highlights the growing trend of LLMs evolving into autonomous scientific agents requiring more sophisticated evaluation methods.

stories.title: When Does On-Policy Interaction Help? Representational Tradeoffs in Value-Based Imitation Learning
stories.author: Dylan J. Foster
bullet_points: The paper addresses limitations in Imitation Learning (IL), specifically the compounding errors of standard Behavior Cloning (BC).
It investigates the role of on-policy interaction in improving IL performance when perfect expert representation is unattainable.
The research focuses on representational tradeoffs, suggesting that interaction strategies can mitigate performance plateaus in IL applications.

stories.title: FriendBench: Benchmarking Dyadic Familiarity Inference in Humans and Multimodal Large Language Models
stories.author: Benjamin Peloquin
bullet_points: Introduces FriendBench, a new benchmark for inferring dyadic familiarity (strangers vs. familiar) from short conversational clips.
Evaluates 26 models from seven companies across text, audio, and video modalities against human panels.
Focuses on the importance of non-verbal behavior in social interaction inference, a key area for multimodal AI.

stories.title: TraceViT: Grounded Trace Supervision for Visual Abstract Reasoning
stories.author: Wei Hua
bullet_points: TraceViT is a new looped visual reasoner designed to improve performance on the Abstract Reasoning Corpus (ARC).
The core innovation is introducing 'Grounded Trace Supervision,' which constrains intermediate refinement steps rather than just the final output.
This addresses a limitation in conventional training methods for visual reasoners, allowing for step-by-step transformation learning.

stories.title: Sign compression for Muon: SignMuon, MuonSign, and the Limits of Error Feedback
stories.author: Alexey Kravatskiy
bullet_points: Introduces SignMuon, a method for compressing the Muon update to one bit per parameter using elementwise sign.
SignMuon achieves superior performance compared to SignSGD while operating under a very low communication budget.
The research highlights limitations in gradient signing placement (before vs. after LMO) and demonstrates cases where signing causes ascent on linear functions.

stories.title: GQ-FSL: Green Quantized Federated Split Learning
stories.author: Lutz Lampe
bullet_points: Addresses energy and resource constraints when deploying DNNs on mobile edge devices.
Proposes Green Quantized Federated Split Learning (GQ-FSL) to reduce overheads in existing Federated Split Learning (FSL).
Focuses on mitigating high energy consumption caused by continuous data exchange in edge learning frameworks.

stories.title: When Does On-Policy Interaction Help? Representational Tradeoffs in Value-Based Imitation Learning
stories.author: Dylan J. Foster
bullet_points: The paper addresses limitations in Imitation Learning (IL), specifically the compounding errors of standard Behavior Cloning (BC).
It investigates the role of on-policy interaction in improving IL performance when perfect expert representation is unattainable.
The research explores representational tradeoffs as a mechanism to enhance agent learning from expert demonstrations.

stories.title: A Human-Centered Validation of the Explainability-Performance Coefficient
stories.author: Luis F. Lago-Fernández
bullet_points: Addresses the critical need for trustworthy Explainable AI (XAI) in high-risk domains.
Proposes a new, model-agnostic metric called the Explainability-Performance Coefficient (EPC) score.
The metric aims to explicitly balance explanation quality with human-centered understanding and model performance.

stories.title: QASP: Query-Adaptive Robust Vector Search Policy
stories.author: Andy Warfield
bullet_points: Addresses the core challenge of balancing high recall and low computational cost in vector search.
Introduces QASP, a novel policy that predicts the full recall progression curve for each query.
Moves beyond average recall metrics to account for significant per-query performance variance.

stories.title: The Parts Are Greater Than the Sum: Automated Task Sequencing for Efficient Training of Multi-Policy LLMs
stories.author: Adam Sobey
bullet_points: Addresses the issue of interference and poor transfer when fine-tuning Multi-Policy LLMs using standard shared LoRA adapters.
Proposes a novel optimization method to overcome the limitations of relying on a single shared optimization path for heterogeneous task sequences.
Contributes to the field of Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) by improving how LLMs adapt to complex, sequential tasks.

stories.title: WCM: A World Critic Model for Vision-Language-Action Reinforcement Learning
stories.author: Xipeng Qiu
bullet_points: The paper introduces 'WCM,' a World Critic Model designed for Vision-Language-Action (VLA) Reinforcement Learning.
It addresses a critical limitation in current RL methods for robotics: the mismatch between single-frame observation reliance and the partially observable nature of robot control.
The model aims to overcome the exponential complexity associated with naively incorporating full observation history into the critic.

stories.title: FriendBench: Benchmarking Dyadic Familiarity Inference in Humans and Multimodal Large Language Models
stories.author: Benjamin Peloquin
bullet_points: Introduces FriendBench, a new benchmark for inferring dyadic familiarity (strangers vs. familiar) from short social interactions.
Tests multimodal LLMs (text, audio, video) against human panels using 20-second ice-breaker clips.
Compares 26 models from seven companies, providing a standardized evaluation of social intelligence in AI.

stories.title: ResKV: Reconstructing Omitted Attention Contributions for Fixed-Budget KV Cache Compression
stories.author: Shuo Shang
bullet_points: The research addresses the critical issue of KV cache compression for efficient long-context LLM inference.
Existing compression methods either permanently discard valuable attention information or risk perturbing retained key/value pairs.
The proposed 'ResKV' method formulates omitted cache information as residual statistics within the softmax attention mechanism.

stories.title: ARB: A Matched Authorship-Rewriting Benchmark Dataset for AI-Text Detector Evaluation
stories.author: Simon Pietro Romano
bullet_points: Introduces ARB, a new benchmark dataset designed to test AI-text detectors under realistic conditions.
Addresses a gap in current research by specifically evaluating detectors when human-authored text is rewritten by LLMs, not just direct LLM output.
The dataset is constructed from 1,800 human source texts, aiming to provide a more nuanced evaluation of authorship detection capabilities.

stories.title: Evidence-Type Competition: When Can Interventional Data Teach Language Models Causal Direction?
stories.author: Xining Xun
bullet_points: The paper investigates the effectiveness of interventional data in teaching language models causal reasoning.
It challenges the assumption that interventional data is always the gold standard for causal learning.
The study finds that in specific scenarios (Simpson's-paradox worlds), increasing interventional data does not improve the model's causal direction.

stories.title: Know It, Act on It: Investigating Memory Utilization in LLM Personalization
stories.author: Emmanuele Chersoni
bullet_points: Investigates the critical issue of knowledge utilization in personalized Large Language Models (LLMs).
Addresses the ambiguity of LLM failure: whether it's a memory retrieval issue or a failure to apply remembered context.
Focuses on memory utilization as a core capability for evolving LLM agents acting as personalized companions.

stories.title: Bridging the Question-Answer Gap in Retrieval-Augmented Generation: Hypothetical Prompt Embeddings
stories.author: Aleksandar Tošić
bullet_points: The paper addresses a core limitation in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems: the style mismatch between user queries and retrieved document text.
It proposes a method involving 'Hypothetical Prompt Embeddings' to improve the alignment between queries and retrieved context.
The research aims to overcome the computational overhead associated with existing runtime solutions like HyDE.

stories.title: AirLLM 70B inference with single 4GB GPU
stories.author: Anon84
bullet_points: The news highlights a significant achievement in AI model deployment: running a 70B parameter LLM.
The key technical feat is achieving this inference using only a single GPU with a limited 4GB of VRAM.
This suggests major advancements in model quantization, optimization, or efficient inference techniques.
